braille.title: Braille Alphabet
braille.intro_text: Welcome to the world of the Braille alphabet, where every letter and number is represented using 6 dots arranged in 2 columns and 3 rows, and counting goes by column (from top to bottom, the first column is 1, 2, and 3, and the second column, in the same order, is 4, 5, and 6 - as shown in the picture). The keyboard letters can also help you: F, D, S = dots 1, 2, and 3 (left hand), J, K, L = dots 4, 5, and 6 (right hand). In other words, for easier orientation, your left hand is for the first column and your right hand for the second; your index finger is for the first, topmost dot in the column (dots 1 and 4), your middle finger is for the second, middle dot in the columns (dots 2 and 5), and your ring finger is for the third, lowest dots in the columns (3 and 6).

braille.express_explanation_text: Here you freely write your own sentences in Braille, sign by sign. You choose the dots with the keys F, D and S (dots 1, 2 and 3) and J, K and L (dots 4, 5 and 6). When you have chosen the dots, press A to hear what you wrote. If it's right, press A once more to confirm it. If only one dot is wrong, delete it with the period key (.); to delete the whole letter, press the colon key (:). If nothing is started, colon deletes the last written sign. For a new word, choose no dots and press A twice - that is a space. The sentence ends when you write a period, question mark or exclamation mark, and then the whole sentence is read back to you. For a capital letter, first write the capital sign (dot 6), then the letter. For a number, first write the number sign (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6); after that the dots are read as digits until the space. The at sign and the slash have two pairs of dots: first you write pair 1, then press H to move to pair 2, and H again takes you back to pair 1. The P key opens the reference, and P again takes you back. You can save your sentence and look at your saved sentences later. The G key turns on the voice command.
braille.sentence_explanation_text: The app tells you a sentence, and you write it in Braille, sign by sign. You can listen to the sentence as many times as you like with "Listen to the sentence", and with "What's next?" you hear the letter or sign that comes next. Writing works just like in "Express Your Thought": choose the dots with F, D and S (dots 1, 2 and 3) and J, K and L (dots 4, 5 and 6), press A to hear the letter, and A again to confirm it. For every correct sign you will hear a success sound. If you write a wrong letter, digit or sign, you will hear a mistake sound right away and can try again. A space is A twice with no dots. Remember: the sentence starts with a capital letter, so first write the capital sign (dot 6), and digits need the number sign first (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6). The sentence ends with a period, question mark or exclamation mark. The period key (.) deletes only the last dot, and the colon key (:) deletes the whole letter. For the at sign and the slash, use the H key for pair 2. The P key opens the reference, and the G key turns on the voice command.

picture_book.title: Learn & Listen
picture_book.intro: Educational picture books are available for different topics across several categories. Choose a category and go through all the picture books, where you'll hear something informative about the topic, with the option to also hear what sound it makes. Once you've gone through all the picture books, a quiz follows to test what you've learned. Good luck!

picture_book.sun_learn: The sun gives us light and warmth. Do not look directly at the sun.
picture_book.tree_learn: Trees make oxygen for breathing. They give shelter to animals.
picture_book.bicycle_learn: Cycling is healthy and eco-friendly. Always wear a helmet and follow traffic rules.

picture_book.water_learn2: Tap water is healthy to drink. If you feel thirsty, your body is reminding you: drink water.

picture_book.book_learn: Reading builds knowledge and imagination. Books and audiobooks are for everyone.

picture_book.fire_learn2: If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. Call for help.
picture_book.phone_learn: Use the phone to stay in touch and in emergencies. Call 112 for emergency, or your local police and fire numbers.
picture_book.phone_learn2: Remember: 112 emergency. Call only when there is real danger. Say your name and where you are.
picture_book.bird_desc: A small animal that flies and sings
picture_book.bird_learn: A bird flies with wings and sings beautiful songs.
picture_book.cow_desc: A farm animal that gives milk
picture_book.cow_learn: A cow gives milk and eats grass in the meadow.
picture_book.wind_desc: Moving air we feel on our skin
picture_book.wind_learn: Wind is moving air. It can be a gentle breeze or a strong storm.
picture_book.clock_desc: A device that shows the time
picture_book.clock_learn: A clock tells us what time it is, so we can be on time.
picture_book.star_desc: A bright point of light in the night sky
picture_book.star_learn: Stars are huge balls of light far away in space. The Sun is a star too.
picture_book.moon_desc: A bright object that shines at night
picture_book.moon_learn: The Moon orbits the Earth, and we see it as a bright ball at night.
picture_book.rocket_desc: A vehicle that flies into space
picture_book.rocket_learn: A rocket flies very fast to carry people and equipment into space.
picture_book.planet_desc: A big ball that orbits a star

picture_book.guitar_learn: A guitar has strings that vibrate when plucked, making beautiful music.

spatial.title: Spatial orientation
spatial.explanation_simon_text: This game trains spatial memory through touch. First tap 'Start sensing' - you'll feel a sequence of vibrations, each direction (up, down, left, right) with its own distinct pattern. Count and remember them carefully, in order. Then, on the cross-shaped pad below, tap the same directions in the same order you felt them. If you want to feel the sequence again before answering, tap 'Sense again'. Each round adds one more step to the sequence - the game has 10 rounds in total.
spatial.explanation_maze_text: This game trains following an invisible path using only touch and vibration. Tap 'Start maze', then place your finger anywhere on the grid below and slowly move it. While your finger is on the correct path, you'll feel a light, short vibration. As soon as you step off the path (hit a 'wall'), you'll feel a stronger vibration and the border will flash red - go back to the last correct spot and keep searching from there. You must trace the path in order, from the start (green square) to the end (gold square) - you can't skip straight to the end. The game has 5 different mazes.
spatial.explanation_radar_text: This game trains finding a hidden object in space. Move your finger across the whole field - the vibrations get more frequent and stronger the closer you get to the hidden object, like a metal detector. At the start, you'll also see a faint glowing circle around the hidden object's location as a visual aid, but that circle becomes less and less visible from round to round, until by the end you'll need to rely on vibration alone. Once you find the object, a key icon appears - drag the key to the lock in the top-right corner to finish the round. The game has 10 rounds.
spatial.explanation_compass_text: This game trains orientation using the cardinal directions. On a phone with a compass sensor: the game tells you a direction (for example 'North'), and you physically turn around in the room until you're facing that way - once you're close enough, you'll feel short vibrations and a circular progress ring will fill up until it's confirmed. On a computer, instead of physically turning, the game shows an icon that moves and rotates through a specific sequence of steps (up, down, left, right, rotate left, rotate right, stay) - watch it carefully, then use the buttons below to repeat the same sequence so the icon ends up in the same final position.
spatial.coming_soon_maze: Virtual maze: trace a path with your finger through an invisible grid - vibration warns you when you leave the path.
spatial.coming_soon_radar: Digital radar: find a hidden object on the screen by following vibrations that get stronger as you get closer.
spatial.coming_soon_compass: Compass and directions: use your phone's compass to find north, south, east and west.

cyber.question1: Should you share your personal information online?
cyber.explanation1: Never share personal information like your address, phone number, or password online. Always ask a parent or teacher first.
cyber.question2: What should you do if a stranger messages you?
cyber.option2b: Tell a parent or teacher and don't reply
cyber.explanation2: If a stranger messages you online, never reply. Always tell a parent or teacher immediately.
cyber.question3: Is it okay to meet someone you met online in person?
cyber.option3a: No, never meet strangers from online
cyber.option3c: Only if they are your age
cyber.explanation3: Never meet someone you met online in person without a parent or teacher present. It's not safe.
cyber.question4: What should you do if someone is being mean to you online?
cyber.option4b: Tell a parent or teacher and block them
cyber.explanation4: If someone is being mean or bullying you online, tell a parent or teacher right away and block that person.

sound_memory.explanation_text: The game has 10 rounds. Each round has 6 cards - 3 pairs of matching sounds (different sounds each round). Tap Start and the cards will open one by one so you can hear and remember the sounds. Then tap two cards at a time to find pairs with the same sound. Every card you open counts as a move.
sound_memory.win: Congratulations! You finished all 10 rounds in {} total moves!

pong.title: Voice Pong
pong.explanation_text: Drag your finger up or down in the dark area to move the paddle. The ball bounces off the top, bottom, and right walls - each bounce plays a tick sound that pans in stereo from the right ear to the left. If the paddle intercepts the ball on the left, that's a hit and the ball speeds up each time. If the ball gets past the paddle - the game ends. Try to get as many hits as you can!
pong.final_summary_survival: You got {} hits before you missed!

melody.explanation_text: The game has 20 rounds in total. You will hear a sequence of sounds, one after another - for example cat, cat, dog, car. First tap Start listening. Then tap the same sounds below in the same order you heard them. Each round can have more sounds in the sequence - from 2 up to 7. At the end you'll see how many rounds you got right and how many wrong.
melody.choose_prompt: Tap the sounds in the order you heard them

rhythm.explanation_text: The game has 10 rounds in total. Tap Play sound to hear the rhythm and carefully count how many beats you heard. If you want to hear it again, tap Play sound again. Then, in the box below, type the number you think is correct, and tap Confirm. If it matches the real number of beats - correct! At the end you'll see how many rounds you got right.

story.explanation_text: Listen to the story - it's always shown on screen too. After each story you have two choices; tap the one you like. You'll hear and see what happens next. When you're ready, tap 'Continue' for the next story - no rushing.
story.intro: Story – your choice. Listen and choose what happens.
story.s1_text: Anna goes to the park. She sees a big tree and a swing. Should she swing or pick flowers?
story.s1_out1: Anna swung and smiled. The air was fresh and it was a lovely day.
story.s1_out2: Anna picked pretty flowers and gave them to Mom. Mom was very happy.
story.s2_text: Mark is thirsty. Should he get water from the fountain or look for juice?
story.s2_out1: Mark drank water and felt better right away. Water is the healthiest.
story.s2_out2: Mark found juice and shared it with his friend. Both were happy.
story.s3_text: Sonia wants to read a book. Should she get a book about animals or about space?
story.s3_out1: Sonia read about lions and elephants. She wanted to see them at the zoo.
story.s3_out2: Sonia read about stars and planets. She wanted to become an astronaut.
